title: wait() errors on exit paths are not classified: a repriced replacement or a status-0 receipt both land in the generic catch, which stays capital-safe through the balance check but records and alerts the wrong outcome

evidence.note: on replacement wait() throws TRANSACTION_REPLACED with reason repriced, cancelled or replaced; repriced still throws (cancelled is false only for repriced)
checkReceipt throws CALL_EXCEPTION for a status-0 receipt
public fallback awaits stx.wait() and returns stx.hash; no error is inspected

catch: re-fetch balanceOf; <= dust is treated as a genuine close with the alert "sell reported failure but position closed"; no sell trades row is inserted on this path (insertTrade is at :1073, before)

sibling_sites_checked: All three wait() sites (:422, :545, :556). The balance-is-truth catch covers every error class: a repriced sell that landed reads balance ~0 and is torn down; a reverted sell reads the balance held and keeps monitoring. Private-leg receipts come from the TX slice (reconciliation), not wait().
severity_rationale: S3: no capital effect found, because the balance re-fetch decides teardown. What remains is a landed (repriced) sell with no sell row, so its proceeds are missing from P&L, and an alert that says the sell failed.
recommendation: On TRANSACTION_REPLACED use err.receipt (check its status) to record the landed sell; on CALL_EXCEPTION record a reverted attempt. Card EXIT-08 (exit bookkeeping). Phase 29.
